records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New retryCount column is method-agnostic in schema and query but semantically SMS-only, so a future feature reusing the column for another reminder method gets cross-method deletion; the deleteMany query should be method-scoped now
records.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the cleanup `deleteMany` was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second branch is not scoped by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so running this SMS scheduler endpoint will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` rows (regardless of method) whose `retryCount > 1`, causing cross-method data deletion.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Concurrent cron runs (overlapping invocations or multiple instances) can both findMany the same unscheduled reminder, both call the SMS provider, and both update retryCount — causing duplicate SMS sends and a retryCount race that can prematurely push a reminder over the deletion threshold; the new retryCount arithmetic makes this pre-existing duplication risk newly destructive.
records.rationale: The diff shows a non-atomic, read-modify-write retryCount update based on a previously fetched value (`data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`) and selection of “unscheduled” reminders via `findMany` without any locking/claiming mechanism. With overlapping executions, two runs can act on the same reminder (both schedule SMS and/or both update retryCount), and the new `deleteMany` condition (`OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`) makes retryCount drift more consequential (potentially leading to early deletion). records.issue_text: [BUG] The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-193 is itself unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 from a concurrent deleteMany or transient DB failure), the exception escapes the catch, aborts the for-loop, leaves every remaining reminder in the batch unscheduled, and returns a 500 instead of { ok: true }, turning per-reminder failures into batch-poisoning failures.
records.rationale: In the new `catch (error)` block, the code does `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ ... })` without its own try/catch (or other guarding). If that update throws (e.g., record missing due to a concurrent `deleteMany`/other worker or transient DB error), the exception will escape the catch block and abort the current async handler, which would stop processing the remaining reminders in the loop. This turns a per-reminder failure into a batch-level failure as described.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `retryCount` is never reset on success, so the counter permanently marks any reminder that ever hit a transient failure, allowing the deleteMany to destroy reminders holding a valid `referenceId`
records.rationale: The diff adds deletion of any reminder with `retryCount > 1` unconditionally (`deleteMany` `where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`). The scheduling loop increments `retryCount` on failure (`data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` both in the `else` branch and `catch`) but on success it only updates `referenceId` and does not reset `retryCount` to 0. Therefore, a reminder that failed twice (retryCount=2) and later succeeds will still match `retryCount > 1` and be deleted on the next run, even if it now has a valid `referenceId`.
